heroDescription: Explore Green Bay's football story through its early survival, championship eras, Lambeau Field and the players who helped shape the Packers.

timeline.title: A team takes shape in Green Bay
timeline.description: Meetings at the Green Bay Press-Gazette in August brought the Packers together. The Indian Packing Company sponsored their first two seasons.

timeline.title: Green Bay joins the league
timeline.description: The Packers entered the American Professional Football Association, which took the NFL name in 1922. Their league debut came two years after the team's founding.

timeline.title: The community buys in
timeline.description: The Green Bay Football Corporation was incorporated in August. Its stock sale helped keep the franchise alive and established the community connection central to its identity.

timeline.title: Three straight NFL championships
timeline.description: Green Bay's first titles came in three consecutive seasons. Before a championship playoff system existed, the league awarded those crowns through the final standings.

timeline.title: Don Hutson changes the passing game
timeline.description: Hutson signed in February and began an eleven-season Packers career. His receiving helped expand the possibilities of an offense in an era still dominated by running.

timeline.title: A new home opens
timeline.description: Green Bay dedicated its new City Stadium on September 29 with a 21–17 win over Chicago. The stadium later became Lambeau Field.

timeline.title: Vince Lombardi arrives
timeline.description: Lombardi became head coach and general manager in January. A 7–5 finish that fall gave the Packers their first winning season in twelve years.

timeline.title: A championship at home
timeline.description: On December 31, Green Bay beat the New York Giants 37–0 in the NFL Championship Game, beginning the title-winning stretch of Lombardi's Packers.

timeline.title: Winners of the first Super Bowl
timeline.description: The 1966 campaign ended with a 35–10 victory over Kansas City on January 15, 1967. Green Bay became the first AFL–NFL world championship game winner.

timeline.title: The Ice Bowl and another Super Bowl
timeline.description: Bart Starr's late sneak beat Dallas in the December 31 Ice Bowl. Green Bay then defeated Oakland in Super Bowl II on January 14, 1968.

timeline.title: The championship returns to Green Bay
timeline.description: The Packers completed the 1996 season by beating New England 35–21 in Super Bowl XXXI on January 26, 1997, ending their long wait for another title.

timeline.title: A road through the playoffs
timeline.description: Wins at Philadelphia, Atlanta and Chicago carried Green Bay to Super Bowl XLV. The Packers beat Pittsburgh 31–25 on February 6, 2011.

eras.title: Lambeau and the early champions
eras.description: Curly Lambeau helped build the club from its local beginnings. His Packers won six NFL championships, including the consecutive titles of 1929, 1930 and 1931.

eras.title: Hutson's passing revolution
eras.description: Don Hutson gave Green Bay a receiving threat defenses struggled to contain. Championships in 1936, 1939 and 1944 extended the club's success into another generation.

eras.title: The Lombardi standard
eras.description: Five NFL titles between the 1961 and 1967 seasons defined this era. Its final two championship seasons also produced victories in the first two Super Bowls.

eras.title: Favre, Rodgers and renewed success
eras.description: Brett Favre helped bring a title back after the 1996 season. Aaron Rodgers later led the offense during the 2010 championship run.

methodology: This independent overview uses the Packers' historical archive and Pro Football Hall of Fame records. Timeline entries and figures link to their sources. Season labels distinguish a football campaign from a Super Bowl played the following calendar year. Players are an across-era selection, not a ranking; NFL championship totals include the Super Bowl victories rather than adding them again.
